key_findings.text: 4 branşın 4 tanesi için yalnızca 4 kaynak dönem (2022 – 2025) yüklendi; bu sayı, yöntemlerin sağlam kanıt için gereksindiği 8 değerinin altındadır: her faktör, oran ve aralık az gözleme dayanır ve yöntemler arasındaki farklar, sonucun kesinliğini değil, sonucun yönteme ne kadar bağlı olduğunu gösterir.
key_findings.title: Yetersiz kanıt

key_findings.text: LIFE: seçilen nihai hasar 107.326.577 TRY; bunun 13.576.168 TRY tutarı (%12,6 nihai hasarın) bugüne kadar gerçekleşen hasarın üzerindedir (IBNR); en büyük pay GROUP_TERM_LIFE branşındadır: 13.576.168 TRY.
key_findings.title: Segment başına rezerv tahmini

key_findings.text: NON_LIFE: seçilen nihai hasar 42.387.389 TRY; bunun 2.449.179 TRY tutarı (%5,8 nihai hasarın) bugüne kadar gerçekleşen hasarın üzerindedir (IBNR); en büyük pay MOTOR_TPL branşındadır: 2.512.208 TRY.
key_findings.title: Segment başına rezerv tahmini

key_findings.text: LIFE: nihai hasar prim oranı 2024 kaynak yılı için %82,0 iken 2025 kaynak yılı için %129,7 değerine yükseldi; yalnızca bu iki kaynak yılı karşılaştırılır: sonuncusu, bir öncekiyle.
key_findings.title: Hasar prim oranı yükseldi

key_findings.text: NON_LIFE: yazılan prim 2024 dönemine göre %41,2 artarak 2025 döneminde 45.783.739 TRY oldu.
key_findings.title: Yazılan prim arttı

key_findings.text: Ödenen hasar zincir merdiven yönteminin, şimdiden gerçekleşmiş tutarın altında nihai hasar verdiği kaynak dönemler: 5 (MOTOR_OD 2025, MOTOR_TPL 2022, 2023, 2024, 2025). Ödeme paterni çok kısa veya muallak hasar karşılıkları yüksek; bu nedenle bu dönemlerin ödenen bazlı tahminleri tek başlarına kullanılmaz.
key_findings.title: Ödenen bazlı nihai hasar gerçekleşenin altında

key_findings.text: Kuyruk faktörü 1,0 iken son gözlenen dönemde gelişim hâlâ 1,050 değerinin üzerinde (MOTOR_TPL paid 36-48 (1,382)); bu branşların nihai hasarı eksik tahmin edilmiş olabilir; kuyruk faktörü varsayım kaydında belirlenebilir.

assumptions: Each claim has one origin period, fixed for the run.
Valuation rows describe the claim as known at their date (as-of rule, CV04).
methods.plain: Builds cumulative and incremental development triangles of paid, incurred, case reserve and claim counts from claim valuations, for any origin and development period and on any basis.
methods.title: Gelişim üçgeni oluşturma

assumptions: Future development of each origin follows the same age-to-age factors as the past.
Origins are comparable; no change in case reserving, payment speed or mix.
No calendar-period effect such as inflation shocks.
methods.plain: Projects each origin's cumulative claims to ultimate with age-to-age factors estimated from the triangle, using volume-weighted, simple or recent-diagonal averages, with optional exclusions.
methods.title: Zincir merdiven (chain ladder)

assumptions: The prior loss ratio is a credible estimate of each origin's ultimate loss ratio.
The chain-ladder pattern describes the share of claims still to emerge.
Earned premium measures exposure consistently across origins.
methods.plain: Ultimate claims as reported claims plus the still-unreported share of an a priori expected ultimate (prior loss ratio times earned premium), the unreported share coming from the chain-ladder pattern.
methods.title: Bornhuetter–Ferguson

assumptions: One expected loss ratio holds for all origins of the group.
The chain-ladder pattern describes reporting, as in MT02.
methods.plain: Bornhuetter–Ferguson with the prior loss ratio estimated from the data: reported claims divided by the premium already "used up" by development, over all origins of a group.
methods.title: Cape Cod

assumptions: The expected loss ratio is a better guide than the claims reported so far.
methods.plain: Ultimate claims as an expected loss ratio times earned premium, ignoring reported claims.
methods.title: Beklenen hasar prim oranı yöntemi

assumptions: The chosen index reflects claims inflation of the line.
Development in real terms is stable, as MT02 assumes.
Future payments of development period k fall at its middle.
methods.plain: Chain ladder on a paid triangle restated to value-date prices, so that development factors are free of past inflation; future payments are re-inflated only with an explicit future inflation assumption.
methods.title: Enflasyondan arındırılmış zincir merdiven

assumptions: Anomalies are rare, so the median and MAD describe normal behaviour.
A reserve that opens or is released is a change of status, not a movement of the same kind as a revision of a running reserve; each kind has its own typical size.
On the log scale the variables are roughly symmetric.
methods.plain: Flags individual payments, case-reserve movements and movements of incurred at a payment that lie far from the typical values of their kind in their segment and line, measured by a z-score built on the median and the median absolute deviation, which outliers cannot distort.
methods.title: Sağlam z-skoru ile anomali işaretleri

assumptions: Anomalous claims are few and differ from the rest on the chosen features.
methods.plain: Scores whole claims by how easily random splits isolate them on a set of claim-level features, and flags the most isolated ones; complements MT08, which looks at single movements.
methods.title: İzolasyon ormanı ile anomali işaretleri

assumptions: Below the maturity threshold the reported claims are too thin to extrapolate by factors alone.
methods.plain: Chooses one ultimate per origin from the methods that ran: chain ladder for origins developed enough, Bornhuetter–Ferguson for immature ones, unless the user selects otherwise.
methods.title: Nihai hasar seçimi

assumptions: The chain-ladder pattern is right (as MT02), and the prior ultimate of MT03 or MT04 is unbiased.
methods.plain: Ultimates that blend the chain ladder and Bornhuetter–Ferguson by maturity: the Benktander (iterated Bornhuetter–Ferguson) estimate, a credibility mix of the chain ladder and Bornhuetter–Ferguson with weight 1 - q^k, as a principled alternative to the hard switch of MT10.
methods.title: Benktander karışımları

assumptions: Expected incremental paid of origin i in development j is n(i) r(j) lambda(i + j): a claim-count measure, a development pattern summing to 1 and a calendar index.
The ultimate claim count n(i) of each origin is known or well estimated.
The pattern sums to 1 over the observed columns, so the method has no development beyond the last column and its ultimates carry no tail.
The future calendar index follows the chosen trend or assumption.
methods.plain: Splits average paid per claim into a development pattern and a calendar-period index (Taylor 1977), so that calendar-year effects such as claims inflation are measured instead of being folded into development factors, then projects with an explicit future index.
methods.title: Ayrıştırma yöntemi (separation)

assumptions: Reported counts develop with a stable pattern (chain ladder on counts).
Severity at value-date prices follows a log-linear trend across origins.
The price index captures most of claims inflation.
methods.plain: Ultimate as ultimate claim count times ultimate severity: counts are developed with the chain ladder on the reported-count triangle, frequency is related to earned exposure, severity is trended from mature origins at value-date prices, and catastrophe claims are projected apart. Also fits the frequency trend that forecasts use (MT27).
methods.title: Frekans–şiddet projeksiyonu

assumptions: Claim sizes of a group are independent draws from one distribution.
Sizes of closed claims are final; open claims' incurred is an estimate.
methods.plain: Fits lognormal, gamma, Weibull and Pareto distributions to individual claim sizes by maximum likelihood, per segment and line, tests the fit, selects one, and gives quantiles, limited expected values and layer costs for limits and reinsurance (MT21).
methods.title: Hasar şiddeti dağılımı uydurma ve uyum iyiliği

assumptions: Censoring at the cut-off is independent of the time to close.
Cox - hazards of the groups are proportional over time.
Cohorts are comparable (no change of handling speed across report years).
methods.plain: Time-to-event curves of claims with censoring: the Kaplan–Meier estimate of the share of claims still open by time since report, and a Cox proportional-hazards model of how line, cause and size change the speed of settlement.
methods.title: Sağkalım analizi (Kaplan–Meier ve Cox)

assumptions: Today's estimate of a mature origin is close to its final cost.
The past cut-offs see the data as it was then.
methods.plain: Measures how good earlier reserve estimates were: the methods and selections are re-run as at earlier cut-offs with only the facts known then (CV04 as-of rule), and their ultimates are compared with today's estimate and, for mature origins, with the developed actual, by method and by horizon.
methods.title: Geçmiş seçimlerin geriye dönük testi
